newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monsengwo to announce initiatives for Zaire peace.
newsitem.headline: Monsengwo to announce initiatives for Zaire peace.

text.p: Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo, potentially a broker between rebel forces and Zaire's ailing president, said on Sunday he would soon take peace initiatives.

"In my role of mediator granted by the constitutional conference, with the support of all the political forces in the country, I will take initiatives in the coming days to find...a peaceful solution to the crisis," he told a news conference.

The personal initiatives, which he did not detail, were aimed at "arriving at a transition which has consensus support and is quick," he said during a stopover on his way back to Kinshasa from the Vatican where he attended a conference.
After a seven-month war rebel forces led by Laurent Kabila are approaching the Zairean capital, putting increasing pressure on President Mobutu Sese Seko to surrender power.
Mobutu, suffering from cancer, has said he will only step down if the process towards democracy and elections in mineral-rich Zaire continues, thus blocking a direct handover to Kabila.
Monsengwo, voted speaker of the transitional parliament on Saturday, could play a crucial role in breaking the deadlock between the warring parties and reaching a settlement.

The post of speaker has been vacant since a combined move by Mobutu followers and the radical UDPS opposition ousted Monsengwo two years ago amid accusations of a lack of neutrality and weakness in the face of Zaire's president of three decades.
However, according to many Zaireans now he is one of the few leading figures with the popular credibility and reputation for neutrality needed to arbitrate among the country's politicians.
His appointment would allow Mobutu the possibility of standing down without leaving a power vacuum in his wake.
According to Zaire's transition constitution, the speaker succeeds the president in the event of his death or incapacity.
First, Monsengwo would have to accept his nomination.
"I will only accept if I have national and international guarantees," he told the news conference.
The archbishop said he also needed the approval of his archbishopic of Kinsangani, of the episcopal conferences of Zaire and Africa, and of the Holy See in Rome.

Asked whether he had already been in touch with the Vatican, he said he would announce his definitive reaction in Kinshasa. All the conditions had to be met before he would accept his election. "It is a package deal."
Monsengwo was due to meet Yves Haesendonck, Belgium's special envoy for the Great Lakes area, on Sunday in Belgium.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman could not say whether details of the meeting would be announced later on Sunday. It was not clear when exactly Monsengwo, who regularly visits Brussels to meet relatives and Belgian officials, would return to Zaire.
Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said Monsengwo could play an important role in ending the conflict through negotiations and without further bloodshed.
"I hope, just like the United States, that we can achieve a 'soft landing'," he said on Belgian television, referring a smooth transition of power in Kinshasa.
Derycke said that Monsengwo could play a useful role on condition that he had wide support.

Saturday's vote, conducted by a show of hands, was marred by a prior walkout by the UDPS party of Etienne Tshisekedi, and it was not clear whether a quorum was achieved nor whether the "consensus" vote would prove binding.
The UDPS on Friday called Monsengwo a "Mobutist."
Monsengwo said he did not fear any opposition, but added that for a succesful role he would need "widespread respect for the democratic will of the people of Zaire."

Belgian Foreign Minister Derycke warned against the replacing of one dictatorship by another and condemned recent mass deaths among Rwandan refugees being repatriated from eastern Zaire, controlled by Kabila's forces.
"What happened in eastern Zaire is unacceptable," he said.
There have been reports that Kabila's Tutsi-dominated troops have mistreated Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire.
Monsengwo said, "What happened in eastern Zaire was a tragegy that could have been avoided."
He attacked the international community for having failed to set up an intervention force late last year to protect and aid the thousands of refugees.
"Now many cry crocodile tears," Monsengwo said of the international outcry over the refugee crisis.
